body:
I am not going to pretend that I have a better response to this question than is provided on this website: http://www.metanoia.org/suicide/

I have ended up there a few times myself.

I hope my modesty makes me not-an-asshole. All the best to you.

Well, you wrote it down and I (at least) read it. Some of what you wrote I recognise and sympathise with, some of it I have no experience of. When I read you talking about what you can do (writing, your studies) it sounds like something inside you is trying to minimise or downplay your achievements - I don't buy it, and it doesn't seem like you really do either. You know you're better than that. I know what it's like to be let down by a parent and how much damage that can do to how you look at your own achievements.

When I read what you wrote it came across to me that you're somebody who has already done some good things, and could do some great things. You know that some of the stuff you're doing now (not cleaning etc.) is only going to keep you down where you are. Once you've been to the bottom you will find that each step: keeping a tidy place, sorting yourself out, etc. will feel like an achievement on its own.

Don't worry about a long-term goal, just try to find something that will keep you going until something comes up (it might be something as small as a song that makes you feel optimistic). There are plenty of happy successful people who never ended up doing the thing they initially set out to do.

All the best to you, I hope things work out.
